issues.description: The template defines the program entry symbol as 'main' (global main) while the provided solution declares 'global _start' and uses a different entry label. This mismatch in the global entry symbol is a structural inconsistency: students following the template expect to implement/execute 'main', but the solution demonstrates using '_start'. This can confuse students about the required entry point and may produce linking/behavior differences when building or running the program.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the entry symbol consistent between template and solution. Either change the solution to export 'global main' and keep the 'main:' label (to match the template and usual C runtime entry), or modify the template and build/link instructions to use '_start' consistently. Also update any documentation/comments so students know which entry point to use when compiling and running the exercise.

issues.description: The program entry symbol is exported with different identifiers across artifacts: the template assembly file declares 'global main' while the solution assembly file declares 'global _start'. Both refer to the program entry/entry-point concept but use different exported names, which can confuse students about which symbol to provide and may cause build/link differences when following the template/Makefile.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent entry symbol name across template and solution. Prefer aligning the solution to the template by changing 'global _start' to 'global main' (or alternatively change the template to export '_start' and ensure the label matches). This removes ambiguity for students following the template and Makefile.
